original_question: For K3 surfaces, prove the Katz-Klemm-Vafa conjecture in every genus and for all curve classes.
target_in_paper: arXiv:1004.3259, section (iv) “On the moduli of K3 surfaces,” Question Q8: “Prove the Katz-Klemm-Vafa conjecture for in all genera and in all classes on K3 surfaces,” with the immediately preceding sentence specifying that the KKV conjecture here concerns λ_g-integrals in the reduced Gromov-Witten theory of a fixed K3 surface.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct object (K3 surfaces), the correct named target (the Katz-Klemm-Vafa conjecture), and the intended scope extension beyond the then-known cases: every genus and all curve classes, not just primitive classes or genus 0.
missing_details: The paper is asking about a fixed nonsingular projective K3 surface over C, not an arbitrary family or a different surface class.
“Curve classes” should be specified as nonzero effective classes β in Pic(S) = H^2(S,Z) ∩ H^{1,1}(S,C), not arbitrary cohomology classes.
The relevant invariants are the reduced Gromov-Witten λ_g-integrals, not the full descendent theory or unreduced Gromov-Witten theory.
One should define R_{g,β}(S) = ∫_[M̄_g(S,β)]^red (-1)^g λ_g, where M̄_g(S,β) is the moduli space of connected genus-g stable maps with no marked points.
To make the conjecture stand-alone, one should define the associated BPS counts r_{g,mα} via the Gromov-Witten potential for multiples of a primitive effective class α.

The full all-class KKV statement includes divisibility-independence: the BPS count r_{g,β} should depend only on the norm square <β,β> = 2h-2 (equivalently, on the arithmetic genus h), not on the divisibility of β.
The exact modular-form prediction should be written explicitly as the product formula for the generating series of the numbers r_{g,h}.
The phrase “all curve classes” should be clarified to mean all effective divisibilities mα with m > 0, including imprimitive classes.
The nearby context in the paper also records the boundary of known results at that time: genus 0 for all classes and all genera for primitive classes.
refined_question: Let S be a nonsingular projective K3 surface over C, and let β ∈ Pic(S) be a nonzero effective curve class. For the reduced Gromov-Witten Hodge integrals R_{g,β}(S) = ∫_[M̄_g(S,β)]^red (-1)^g λ_g, define for each primitive effective class α ∈ Pic(S) the Gromov-Witten potential F_α(λ,v) = Σ_{g≥0} Σ_{m>0} R_{g,mα}(S) λ^{2g-2} v^{mα}, and define BPS counts r_{g,mα} by the identity F_α(λ,v) = Σ_{g≥0} Σ_{m>0} r_{g,mα} λ^{2g-2} Σ_{d>0} (1/d)(sin(dλ/2)/(λ/2))^{2g-2} v^{dmα}. Prove the full Katz-Klemm-Vafa conjecture: the numbers r_{g,β} depend only on h = 1 + <β,β>/2 (equivalently, not on the divisibility of β), and the resulting invariants r_{g,h} satisfy the formal power series identity Σ_{g≥0} Σ_{h≥0} (-1)^g r_{g,h}(y^{1/2} - y^{-1/2})^{2g} q^h = Π_{n≥1} 1/((1-q^n)^20(1-yq^n)^2(1-y^{-1}q^n)^2).
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, determine all reduced λ_g-integrals R_{g,β}(S) for every genus g and every nonzero effective class β on a fixed projective K3 surface, including all imprimitive classes, by proving that the associated BPS counts are divisibility-independent and are governed by the above modular product formula.
justification: The supplied arXiv paper 1004.3259 is a short open-problems note, so the nearest official target is Q8 rather than a theorem or conjecture with full notation. The surrounding sentences make clear what Q8 is actually about: the Katz-Klemm-Vafa conjecture concerning λ_g-integrals in the reduced Gromov-Witten theory of a fixed K3 surface, with genus 0 already known for all classes and all genera already known for primitive classes. Because Q8 names the conjecture but does not restate it formally, the refined version makes the question stand-alone by importing the precise reduced-integral/BPS formulation used in the cited K3 papers: first the reduced Hodge integrals and primitive-class formulation from arXiv:1001.2719, and then the full all-divisibility formulation from arXiv:1404.6698, where the conjecture is written as divisibility-independence plus the explicit modular-form product formula.
